channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Russia sharply restricts cash exports to Kazakhstan and other EAEU countries
item.description: Russia has significantly limited the export of cash to Kazakhstan and other member states of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). The specific details and reasons for this sharp restriction were not provided in the source.

item.title: Kabul women face double fares and refusal of service on public transport
item.description: Women and girls in Kabul report facing restrictions and problems on public transport, including drivers refusing service or demanding double fares. They state that gender-based restrictions extend to social services, forcing women to pay more and endure longer waits for transport.

item.title: Mother Sentenced to 1.5 Years of Freedom Restriction for Negligent Homicide of Infant
item.description: A court in the Akmola region sentenced a mother to 1 year and 6 months of restricted freedom for the negligent homicide of her infant. The woman, intoxicated, fell asleep while breastfeeding, leading to the baby's death from suffocation.

item.title: Members of People's Council inspect rural infrastructure and schools in Abai region
item.description: Representatives of the People's Council of Kazakhstan have begun regional inspections, starting with the Abai region. The working group, led by Lyazzat Chinkisbayeva, is focusing on the quality of rural infrastructure and conditions in schools, documenting issues for legislative review.

item.title: Kazakhstan's grain harvest nears 20 million tons despite dry weather, exceeding average yields
item.description: Kazakhstan's grain harvest has reached nearly 20 million metric tons by late September, despite dry conditions in some areas. The Agriculture Ministry anticipates the final yield will surpass the long-term average, with exports already showing an increase compared to the previous year.

item.title: German D.A.R. Metall AG to Invest in Waste Recycling in Alatau
item.description: German company D.A.R. Metall AG is considering a project to recycle household and industrial waste in Alatau. The company also expressed interest in new projects with Qarmet. This follows a meeting between Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and D.A.R. Metall AG's Chairman Christian Artner, discussing the company's operations in Kazakhstan and potential joint ventures.

item.title: Kazakh Family's Company Earns $42.7 Million from Gold Mine in First Half
item.description: AltynGold, a company owned by a prominent Kazakh family, reported earnings of $42.7 million in the first half of the year, a 58% increase. The company plans to boost the Sekisovskoye field's capacity to 1 million tons of ore annually. Revenue rose 64.6% to $115.2 million, with record half-year profits.

item.title: Moody's affirms Kazakhstan's credit rating with a stable outlook
item.description: International rating agency Moody's has affirmed Kazakhstan's sovereign credit rating at Baa1 with a "Stable" outlook. The agency cited the country's strong fiscal position, low government debt, and high servicing capacity as reasons for the decision.

item.title: Official in Atyrau region fired over misuse of 600 million tenge for housing
item.description: The head of the construction department in the Kurmangazy district of Atyrau region was dismissed for fraud involving the purchase of housing worth 600 million tenge. The acquired apartments were found to be unsuitable for living, lacking gas supply.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Meets with D.A.R. Metall AG Chairman Christian Artner
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Christian Artner, Chairman of D.A.R. Metall AG, to discuss developing partnerships and adopting German technologies in industry and ecology. They emphasized the importance of the metallurgy sector and potential joint projects in metal processing and waste recycling.

item.title: EBRD to Fund Khujand Water and Sewerage System Renovation with €32 Million
item.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is set to provide €32 million for the renovation of the water and sewerage system in Khujand. Additionally, a further €70 million may be allocated for the improvement of the water supply system in the Mastchoh district.

item.title: Officials Punished in Atyrau Region for Discrediting Public Service
item.description: Two officials in the Atyrau region were punished for misconduct related to budget spending on construction projects. One was dismissed for purchasing apartments not connected to gas networks, while another received a warning for paying a contractor for uncompleted work.

item.title: Uzbekistan Parliament Approves Life Sentence for Crimes Against Children
item.description: The Parliament of Uzbekistan has approved a life sentence for individuals convicted of crimes against children. This legislative change aims to impose the strictest penalties for such offenses.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Denies Forecast of Sharp Increase in Beef Prices
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture stated there is no basis for predictions of a sharp increase in beef prices. Vice Minister Nazgul Khatepova confirmed domestic demand is fully met by local production, with 434,000 tons produced last year and production increasing this year.

item.title: United Front Claims Attack on Taliban Governor's Office in Ghor
item.description: The 'United Front of Afghanistan' claimed responsibility for an attack on the Taliban governor's office in Firozkooh, Ghor province. A statement reported one Taliban guard killed and eight wounded, with the governor reportedly unharmed. Local Taliban officials have not commented.

item.title: Over 150 Rights Advocates Urge Kazakhstan Not to Extradite Russian Activists
item.description: More than 150 human rights defenders, academics, journalists, and public figures have called on Kazakhstan to halt the extradition of activists Yulia Emelianova and Mansur Movlaev to Russia. They cite a high risk of imprisonment, mistreatment, and politically motivated prosecution in Russia. The advocates emphasized Kazakhstan's obligations under international conventions against torture and political rights.

item.title: Afghan Journalist Missing in Islamabad; Police Refuse to Investigate
item.description: An Afghan journalist, Qasim Hashimi, has been missing in Islamabad for three months. His wife, Hosina Hashimi, fears eviction due to unpaid rent and lives in constant fear for her family's safety. She states police have not investigated his disappearance, adding to their distress after fleeing the Taliban.

item.title: Almaty Yeast Plant Sells Equipment to Russian Subsidiary of Global Market Leader
item.description: The Almaty Yeast Plant is selling its equipment to the Russian subsidiary of a global market leader. The specific details of the transaction and the identity of the global market leader were not provided in the source.

item.title: Kazakh President Meets with Wilo Group Chairman to Discuss Investment
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Oliver Hermes, head of the German technology group Wilo, during an official visit to Germany. Tokayev praised Wilo's investment in a production facility in the Almaty region and its use of Kazakhstan as a platform for Central Asian markets. He emphasized deepening localization and developing local potential.

item.title: US Dollar Trades at 439.3 Tenge on Kazakhstan Stock Exchange
item.description: The US dollar closed at 439.27 tenge on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange, weakening by 1.93 tenge against the national currency. The average weighted exchange rate reflected this shift following Tuesday's trading session.

item.title: Putin Restricts Cash Exports from Russia to EAEU Countries, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Azerbaijan
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has banned individuals from taking more than one million rubles (approximately $11,800) in cash out of Russia to EAEU member states, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Azerbaijan. Legal entities and individual entrepreneurs are also prohibited from exporting rubles to these countries.

item.title: Astana Pensioner Loses Over 3 Million Tenge to Online Scammers Posing as Telecom and Security Officials
item.description: An elderly woman in Astana lost over 3 million tenge (approximately $4,668) to online scammers. The fraudsters, posing as employees of Kazakhtelecom, the National Security Committee, and the National Bank, convinced her to transfer funds to a 'safe account'. She was later involved in defrauding another pensioner.

item.title: Mavlana Askarbekov Sentenced to Two Years for Facebook Posts Criticizing China
item.description: Mavlana Askarbekov has been sentenced to two years in prison for his Facebook posts. Shortly before his arrest, he actively published content criticizing Chinese businesses operating in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Tajikistan and Qatar Discuss New Investment Projects and "Diyori Dushanbe" Implementation
item.description: Tajikistan's State Committee for Investments chairman met with Qatari Diar CEO in Doha to discuss attracting Qatari investments, joint projects, and the "Diyori Dushanbe" project. The visit aims to boost economic cooperation.

item.title: Almaty Airport Secures $670 Million for Expansion Phase
item.description: Almaty Airport has secured $670 million in funding for its next expansion phase. This investment will support the airport's development and enhance its capacity to handle increased air traffic.

item.title: Kazakhstan producers to be integrated into Deutsche Bahn supply chain
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with German company executives in Berlin to discuss integrating Kazakh producers into Deutsche Bahn's supply chain. They also discussed cooperation in passenger and freight transport, including the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev meets with Deutsche Bahn group leaders
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with leaders of the Deutsche Bahn group, praising the company's contribution to modernizing the national railway sector. Discussions included integrating Kazakh producers into the supply chain and cooperation in passenger and freight transport.

item.title: Senator sends inquiry to Uzbek Prime Minister on child protection from violence
item.description: Senator Malika Kodirxonova has sent an inquiry to Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov regarding measures to prevent individuals convicted of crimes against children from working in child-related organizations. The inquiry seeks data on the registry of offenders and its usage.

item.title: Taliban Minister of Industry and Trade visits Belarus for economic cooperation
item.description: Nouruddin Azizi, the Taliban's Minister of Industry and Trade, has traveled to Belarus with a delegation. The visit aims to participate in an international industry exhibition and expand economic and trade ties between Afghanistan and Belarus. Azizi is scheduled to meet with Belarusian ministers to discuss trade, economic, and industrial cooperation.

item.title: IOM: 6.4 Million Afghan Returnees Face Unemployment and Basic Needs Shortages
item.description: An IOM assessment found 69% of 6.4 million Afghan returnees are unemployed and 54% cannot meet basic needs. The report indicates 77% live in temporary shelters, 14% were evicted, and 43% lack documentation for services. Food, shelter, and cash assistance are pressing needs, with many lacking healthcare and water access.

item.title: Putin bans cash exports exceeding 1 million rubles to EAEU and other countries
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has prohibited the export of cash exceeding 1 million rubles (approximately $11,887) from Russia to Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) member states, as well as Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. The decree also forbids legal entities and individual entrepreneurs from exporting any amount of cash to these countries.

item.title: Zelensky Claims North Korea Preparing to Send 10,000 More Soldiers to Russia
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that North Korea is preparing to send an additional 10,000 soldiers to Russia. He urged countries whose citizens are recruited for the war to resist this action.

item.title: Central Asian Digital Trade Forum Held in Dushanbe
item.description: A forum on digital trade in Central Asia convened in Dushanbe, bringing together government bodies, international organizations, financial institutions, and businesses. Discussions focused on practical approaches to paperless trade, e-commerce, digital logistics, and regional integration. The concept of a "Unified Digital Trade Footprint" was a key topic, aiming to streamline trade processes.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host CIS Regional Forum on Digital Development
item.description: Dushanbe will host a regional International Telecommunication Union (ITU) forum for CIS countries on September 29-30, 2026. The event, focusing on digital development, will include discussions on telecommunication infrastructure, digital transformation, cybersecurity, and network resilience. Tajikistan will be the host nation for the first time.

item.title: Kyrgyz activist sentenced to two years for inciting ethnic hatred on Facebook
item.description: A Bishkek court sentenced civil activist Mavlyan Askarbekov to two years in prison on September 29. He was found guilty of inciting racial, ethnic, national, religious, or interregional hatred through his Facebook posts. The state security committee investigated the case. Askarbekov denied the charges and had been in custody since June.

item.title: Kazakhstan grain shipments to Afghanistan increase 4.4 times in eight months
item.description: Grain shipments from Kazakhstan to Afghanistan surged 4.4 times to 655,000 tons in the first eight months of the year, according to the Transport Vice Minister. Kazakhstan transported 9.3 million tons of grain by rail during the period, a 13% increase year-on-year.

item.title: Samanid-era stucco panel fragments discovered in Bukhara archaeological site
item.description: Fragments of stucco panels with Kufic inscriptions, belonging to a congregational mosque from the Samanid era (9th-10th centuries), were found at the Shahriston archaeological site in Bukhara. The discovery was made by an Uzbek-US international archaeological expedition. Restoration and conservation work is underway.

item.title: Octobank participates in SIBOS 2026 as the sole Uzbek bank with its own stand
item.description: Octobank is participating in SIBOS 2026, being the only bank from Uzbekistan to have its own dedicated stand at the event. The information was provided by Daryo.uz.

item.title: Taliban Arrest Former Kandahar Anti-Narcotics Chief and His Son
item.description: Local sources report the Taliban arrested Gul Mohammad Shukran, former head of Kandahar's anti-narcotics department, and his son. Shukran had been working at a private hospital since the republic's fall. The reason for their arrest remains unclear. This follows an increase in Taliban arrests of former government employees.

item.title: Infrastructure Alone Insufficient for Trans-Caspian Corridor Development
item.description: Modernizing the Trans-Caspian International Transport Corridor (TITR) could triple transit volumes by 2040, halve delivery times, and create 2 million jobs, according to a World Bank report. The study covers nine countries. Reforms enhancing trade and transport efficiency are crucial alongside infrastructure investment for full potential.
